findings.message: Approved blueprint item missing: specs/content/gnas-301/content-spec.md:406-408 requires the summative assessment to include one Analyze-or-higher item comparing two waste streams (household vs hospital) for hazards and handling. No such item exists in docs/semester-1/gnas-301/unit-02/unit-assessment.mdx (ERQ 3 at :126-128 covers hospital risk waste without the household comparison; MCQ 9 touches the mixed heap at Apply only) or in the three topic summative tasks. Unit 1 implemented its analogous requirement (unit-01 ERQ 2 traces a local issue to regional and global scales). Repair request: rework ERQ 3, or restructure within the 5-ERQ budget, so the learner must compare a household waste stream with a hospital risk stream on hazards and handling at Analyze or above, and align its analytic rubric.

RRQ 2 mark scheme arithmetic is inconsistent: docs/semester-1/gnas-301/unit-02/unit-assessment.mdx:161-162 allocates Marks (4) as 1 per resource (four resources = 4 marks) plus 1 for at least two correct challenges, which allocates 5 marks against a 4-mark total, so a marker cannot apply it consistently. Repair request: either raise the total to 5 marks or fold the challenge into per-resource marks (for example 1 per resource named with its challenge).

MCQ key skew: 9 of the 10 correct options are b (only MCQ 6 keys c). Each item is individually correct and unambiguous, but the key pattern is gameable by a test-wise student. Repair request: redistribute correct options across a-d at the next bank revision.

Bloom labels versus actual demand: MCQ 3 is labelled (Apply) but only requires recalling the Chachro study finding (Remember/Understand); ERQ 3 is labelled (Evaluate) while its stem (explain the categories, the rules broken, who bears the risk) sits at Understand/Analyze. Repair request: relabel from the thinking actually required, per the G3 rubric.

Further reading uses bare URLs as link text (topic-01.mdx:152/156/158, topic-02.mdx:166/168, topic-03.mdx:170/172), the same advisory the Unit 1 render inspection recorded. Repair request: use descriptive link text (for example the DOI string or WHO Drinking-water fact sheet).

The global 97/3 salt-fresh split, the ice/groundwater share and the 1,700/1,000 cubic-metre stress/scarcity thresholds (topic-01.mdx:39-44, 64-66) are presented without a stated source, contrary to the spec best-practice note to present water figures as approximate shares with a stated source (content-spec.md:456-460). The values are standard and stated as approximate shares with no false precision, but they are unsourced. Repair request: cite a source for the distribution split and the per-capita thresholds or ground them in a bound source.

U2-05 hospital and industrial waste handling rules (colour-coded segregation at generation, sharps containers that cannot be reopened, autoclaving or incineration, licensed handlers, manifests; topic-03.mdx:69-89) are standard practice but are carried by no verified bound source: they rest on general knowledge plus title-level declared support (park-park, D-2026-0001, owner-confirmed G-2026-23). The declaration in sources/unit-02.md:33-38 is honest and complete, so this does not fail the sources criterion, but the unit's own admission that its WHO- and registry-verified sources do not carry these principles leaves them uncorroborated within the bundle. Repair request at next revision: bind a verifiable open-access healthcare-waste management source (for example WHO guidance) for the U2-05 handling rules.

Sanitation is on the spec Unit 2 key-terms list (content-spec.md:394-395) but is used in topic-02.mdx:65-67 without a glossary link or definition; the other nine key terms are glossary-linked at first use. Repair request: glossary-link the first prose use or define it inline.
